children: Boardroom pay growth at European financial services companies outstripped North American peers last year, narrowing the transatlantic pay gap, according to data from consulting company EY.
European nonexecutive remuneration rose 10% in 2025, more than double the 4.5% increase in North America and 4.7% rise in the Asia-Pacific region, EY said in a report published Monday.
Average remuneration in Europe reached $314,148 in 2025, compared to $350,847 in North America and $273,006 in Asia Pacific.
The gap between European and North American boards narrowed, as European boardrooms now pay 10.5% less on average compared with a 15% gap in 2024. In absolute terms, the disparity slimmed 27%.
"In a 12-month period, Europe's financial services firms have invested in board talent in a major way, responding to cross-border competition for skills and experience," said EY's Omar Ali.
The authors of the report said a number of senior hires in Europe, combined with increased international competition, added notable momentum to European remuneration.

Despite narrowing the regional gap to North America, Europe still has the widest gender pay gap across all three regions, EY said. Female nonexecutive directors in Europe earned 39% less than males, compared with gaps of 30% in Asia Pacific and 7.1% in North America.
However among directors under 50, average pay is broadly equal between women and men. Women make up just over half of the under-50 cohort, EY added.

The premium paid for the board chair role increased in 2025, as the global average chair remuneration climbed 14% to $755,136 compared with a 5.8% rise to $296,706 for other board nonexecutive directors, according to the EY data.
The wealth and asset management sector saw the strongest climb in average nonexecutive pay, continuing a long-term trend.
Wealth and asset management pay grew 11.5%, compared with a 6.5% increase in insurance and a 4.5% growth in banking.
The report tracked 2025 remuneration data for 217 companies, and included 1,974 nonexecutive directors.
